name: Sketching
description:
Sketching uses rapid visual representations to explore, externalise and communicate ideas. In design, sketches are not simply illustrations of decisions already made; they are tools for thinking through form, relationships, interactions and alternatives.

Their provisional quality makes ideas easier to change and supports exploration before detailed commitment.
whenToUse: Use sketching throughout design whenever visualising an idea can help you think about it, compare alternatives or communicate it to others.
steps: Define the question you are exploring.
Focus on relationships and ideas rather than visual polish.
Compare sketches and identify promising elements.
Increase detail only as the questions become more specific.
lookOutFor: Drawing skill should not determine the perceived quality of an idea.
A polished sketch can discourage change too early.
Use annotations where a drawing could otherwise imply functionality or certainty that has not been resolved.

resources.citation: Buxton, B. (2007). *Sketching User Experiences*. Morgan Kaufmann.
Goldschmidt, G. (1991). “The Dialectics of Sketching.” *Creativity Research Journal*, 4(2), 123–143.
